newsitem.title: USA: Fleet says will sell insurance in Conn.
newsitem.headline: Fleet says will sell insurance in Conn.

text.p: Fleet Financial Group Inc said Thursday it has received court approval to market insurance products throughout Connecticut.
Boston-based Fleet said in a statement it expected to complete Connecticut licensing requirements within a few weeks, and that sales would begin within 90 days.
It said the U.S. District Court in Connecticut recently ruled in the bank's favor.
Fleet will initially sell term life, disability income, and long-term care insurance. It expects to follow with homeowners, auto insurance and other products.
Fleet already has authority to sell varying insurance products in all other New England states, as well as New York, New Jersey and Florida.

U.S. Judge Janet Bond Arterton's ruling, handed down May 23, caps a three-year court battle launched by Shawmut Bank and carried on by its sucessor, Fleet, to push national banks into insurance sales.
Banks have long viewed the sale of insurance as a promising source of revenue.
Connecticut insurance agent groups have opposed banks selling insurance.
The agent groups say that the banks will take away business, and also argue that banks do not have long-standing expertise in selling insurance.
Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal had opposed Fleet in the court case.
"We are reviewing the decision and consulting with state regulators as to whether any future action should be taken," Blumenthal said in a statement. He did not elaborate.
The court ruling applies to all national banks in Connecticut, but not to those with only a state charter.
